text.p: Francois Santoni, head of the separatist Corsican National Liberation Front -- Historical Branch (FLNC) underground movement surrendered to police on the Mediterranean island on Monday, France-Info radio said.
No further details were immediately available.
The fugitive leader's reported surrender came hours after police detained his close friend, Marie-Helene Mattei, a lawyer who specialised in defending separatists before French courts.

The FLNC is held responsible by police for dozens of bomb attacks against government and other buildings on the island in the past few months. Santoni is the head of the Cuncolta Naziunalista party, the legal wing of the outlawed FLNC.
The attacks, which have cut deeply into the picturesque island's tourist trade, have caused few casualties since virtually all are carried out at night on empty premises.
Mattei was detained by police in connection with a bomb attack on a luxury golf club which investigators believe was linked to an extortion attempt by separatists.
